title: Group Sales Note on Household Accounts Holding Several Resort Lodging Reservations
content:
A household account carries a separate Resort Lodging reservation for every unit it takes, so a family booking two residences side by side holds two reservations with two folios and two deposits. The account may carry several live reservations at once up to the number this charter allows, which is 5, counting reservations that are on hold, awaiting their deposit, firm or in occupation. Once the account reaches a unit type's group block threshold for one set of dates, the reservations are handled as a group block by the group sales desk rather than added one by one at the service desk. Two live reservations of the same unit type for the same lead guest over the same arrival date are never opened; the second is treated as a duplicate of the first and the household is asked whether they meant a second unit for a different lead guest.

## Which reservations count towards the limit

A reservation counts towards the limit of 5 while it is on hold, while it is awaiting its deposit, while it is firm and while the party is in occupation. A reservation that has been given up, that was never claimed, that has been departed or that has been closed does not count.

## What makes a second reservation a duplicate

The test for a duplicate is made on the collective's own records before the reservation is opened, not on what the household says, and it turns on three things standing together: the same household account, the same lead guest name and the same arrival date, on a reservation of the same unit type that is itself still live. Where all of those coincide, the second reservation is a duplicate of the first. Where the second reservation is for a different unit type, at a different mountain, in a different unit, or for a different lead guest or a different arrival date, it is a second reservation in its own right and not a duplicate.

### Two hypothetical accounts

A household holds a firm Slopeside Studio reservation for the 5th of February with a lead guest named on it, and asks for a second Slopeside Studio for the 5th of February with the same lead guest named again. The three tests coincide on a live reservation, so the second is a duplicate of the first and the household is asked whether they meant a second unit for a different lead guest.

A household holds the same firm Slopeside Studio reservation and asks for a Slopeside Two-Bedroom Residence for the 5th of February with the same lead guest. The unit type differs, so the second is not a duplicate; it opens as its own reservation with its own folio and its own deposit, and the account then carries two of the 5 live reservations allowed.
